items.fullSentence: Je ne fais pas de tennis.

whyWrong.du: du survives only in positive sentences — after ne … pas it collapses to de.
whyWrong.le: le stays only after liking verbs (aimer, adorer, détester) — faire takes de in the negative.
whyWrong.des: des also collapses to de after ne … pas.

whyWrong.de: after aimer/adorer/détester the article does NOT collapse — le stays.
whyWrong.du: du is for doing/consuming some of something — liking takes le.
whyWrong.un: likes and dislikes are about tennis in general — le, not un.

items.fullSentence: Il n'y a pas de café.

whyWrong.du: il y a du café, but after ne … pas the du collapses to de.
whyWrong.le: le survives negation only after liking verbs — il y a takes de.
whyWrong.de la: café is masculine, and in the negative everything collapses to plain de anyway.

whyWrong.de: aimer keeps its article under negation — la stays.
whyWrong.de la: de la is partitive (doing/consuming) — liking takes plain la.
whyWrong.une: general likes take the definite article — la natation.

items.fullSentence: Nous ne mangeons pas de chocolat.

whyWrong.du: manger du chocolat — but ne … pas turns du into de.
whyWrong.le: le would need a liking verb; manger takes de in the negative.
whyWrong.au: au means 'to the / with' — not an amount of chocolate.

whyWrong.de: after aimer the article survives — les stays.
whyWrong.des: des collapses to de after pas — but aimer doesn't use des at all: les.
whyWrong.un: bonbons is plural and general — les.

whyWrong.de: before a vowel de elides — d'eau.
whyWrong.de l': the partitive de l' collapses to d' after ne … pas.
whyWrong.l': l' survives negation only after liking verbs — il y a takes d'.

items.fullSentence: Tu ne fais pas de musique ?

whyWrong.de la: de la collapses to plain de after ne … pas.
whyWrong.la: la survives negation after aimer — faire takes de.
whyWrong.du: musique is feminine, and the negative collapses everything to de anyway.
